body.heading: Meet a snail
paragraphs: After rain or on a damp morning, look for a snail on a wall, a path edge, or a leaf. Snails carry their home — their shell — on their backs wherever they go.
A snail moves on one big, soft foot. It makes slippery slime to glide on, which is why it leaves a shiny trail behind.

body.heading: Time the glide
paragraphs: Ask your adult to start a timer for one minute. Mark where the snail starts, then mark where it reaches when the minute ends.
Snails are famous for being slow, but they never stop. Measure the snail's minute journey with your finger. Could an ant have gone further? Probably — but the snail is not racing anyone.

body.heading: Leave it in peace
paragraphs: If you placed a leaf near the snail, it may stop for a nibble. Snails eat leaves and help clean up the garden.
When you say goodbye, leave the snail where it is. It knows its own way home — after all, it carries it.

takeaway: A snail glides slowly on one soft foot, carrying its home, and it gets there in the end.
safetyNotes: Be gentle — never pull a snail off a surface, as that can hurt it. Wash your hands well after being near snails.
screenFreeExtension: Move like a snail across the room, as slowly as you can, and see who can go slowest without stopping.
